Volume I · The Dispatches Cloverdale, Sonoma County 266 Acres · Asti Road

Ground Truth

A documentary record of the 266-acre Masonite wood-treatment and former Louisiana-Pacific mill site south of Cloverdale — what was made here, what still lies in the ground, and what is now proposed to be built over it.

Compiled · Spring 2026

Eighteen dispatches make up this record. The first thirteen set down what the public documents say; the last five let you see the ground itself. Start anywhere — but if you read only one, read the chronicle.

I · In the record

What the documents say

  • The Chronicle · 266 Acres South of Town The full documentary history, from Masonite’s wood-treatment plant to the 605-unit Esmeralda village now proposed for the parcel. groundtruth.watch/chronicle
  • Telling the Ground Truth A plain-language telling for the neighbors of what the record actually means. groundtruth.watch/telling
  • Sources & Documents Every public record the chronicle rests on, with notes on where each one lives. groundtruth.watch/sources
  • The Public Record Every comment on the 2009 Alexander Valley Resort EIR, paraphrased into plain language with the City’s responses kept verbatim. groundtruth.watch/comments
  • We Asked the Binder Plain answers to the questions a neighbor actually asks, drawn from the documentary record. groundtruth.watch/faqanda
  • Write to City Hall A builder that turns what you care about into a letter to the City, in your own words, ready to send. groundtruth.watch/write
  • The Monitoring Record Six views of the groundwater data the state collected for about two decades—then stopped: the sampling timeline, the exceedances, how deep it sits, and what the closure left unmeasured. groundtruth.watch/record
  • The Oak Tree A response to the June 2026 San Francisco Chronicle profile of the project—what the piece didn’t ask, answered from the regulatory record. groundtruth.watch/oaktree
  • The Scale of It 605 homes and 200 hotel rooms, set against every other residential project in Cloverdale’s modern planning record. groundtruth.watch/scale
  • The Environmental Review One EIR, certified in 2009. Two addenda since. A third now sought for a far larger project—read across, side by side. groundtruth.watch/review
  • The Site Dossier A documented timeline of the wood-treatment and sawmill site, built entirely from public records. groundtruth.watch/history
  • The Covenant A covenant is only as good as the memory of it—a thought experiment in how a recorded deed restriction fails by forgetting, not by breach. groundtruth.watch/forgetting
  • The Risk Threshold What a cancer-risk threshold counts, who sets it, and what the Esmeralda plan asks to change about the one adopted in 2009—with two tools you can move by hand. groundtruth.watch/threshold
II · On the ground

What the parcel shows

  • The Wells An interactive map of the 45 monitoring wells, their contamination readings, and the two wells destroyed weeks before the case closed. groundtruth.watch/destroyed
  • A View from Above Historical aerials of the parcel set against the 2026 Esmeralda site plan, year by year. groundtruth.watch/viewing
  • Molalla / Masonite Mill, 1965 A single annotated aerial of the plant at work, marking the ground the 2013 covenant now restricts. groundtruth.watch/underfoot
  • Cloverdale, 2018 / 2024 A side-by-side wipe of USDA imagery six years apart, the do-nothing baseline the proposal is measured against. groundtruth.watch/status-quo
  • About Construction Dust An interactive wind model of how contaminated dust can drift off-site during Phase 1 grading. groundtruth.watch/dust

About this index

This is the front page of the Unraveling project — a citizen’s record of the 266 acres south of Cloverdale. The dispatches above are compiled from the Cloverdale Reveille archive, the Regional Water Board’s GeoTracker file, the project Environmental Impact Report and its addenda, and contemporary reporting. Mistakes will most certainly be made.

The record will grow as the regulatory and entitlement processes unfold. If you hold a public document, comment letter, or piece of correspondence that belongs here, the compilers welcome the addition. Errors of fact, omission, or emphasis should be reported back so that later versions can correct them. Distribute freely; correct generously.
